# CASE ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM
**Case ID:** 43B70C45 | **Jurisdiction:** Telangana — GST Tribunal / High Court of Telangana | **GSTIN:** 36AABCU9603R1ZX

---

## 1. CASE SUMMARY

The registered taxpayer bearing GSTIN 36AABCU9603R1ZX, registered in Hyderabad, Telangana (State Code 36), has received a show cause notice (SCN) under Section 74 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. Section 74 proceedings are invoked where the revenue authority alleges short payment, non-payment, erroneous refund, or wrongful availment of Input Tax Credit attributable to **fraud, wilful misstatement, or suppression of facts**. The notice mandates a formal reply within the statutory period. No party names, demand quantum, or tax period have been provided; the analysis proceeds on the statutory framework applicable to all S.74 proceedings. The immediate procedural posture is pre-adjudication: the noticee must respond before the adjudicating authority passes an order under S.74(9).

---

## 2. KEY LEGAL ISSUES

- **Primary Issue:** Whether the conditions precedent for invoking S.74 — specifically fraud, wilful misstatement, or suppression of facts — are established on the facts, and whether the demand quantum is legally sustainable.
- **Secondary Issues:**
  - Whether the extended limitation period of five years (S.74 read with S.73) applies, and whether the SCN was issued within that window.
  - Whether Input Tax Credit (ITC) was lawfully availed under S.16, and whether any reversal demand is maintainable.
  - Whether the SCN specifies the grounds with sufficient particularity to satisfy natural justice (absence of which renders the notice void).
  - Whether the taxpayer is entitled to reduced penalty under S.74(5) by paying tax and interest before adjudication.

---

## 3. APPLICABLE LAWS & PROVISIONS

| Act / Regulation | Section / Rule | Relevance to This Case |
|---|---|---|
| CGST Act, 2017 | S.74 | Primary charging provision — SCN alleging demand due to fraud/misstatement; adjudication framework |
| CGST Act, 2017 | S.73 | Distinguishes cases without fraud; determines correct section and limitation period |
| CGST Act, 2017 | S.16 | Governs ITC eligibility conditions; unlawful availment is primary trigger for S.74 proceedings |
| CGST Act, 2017 | S.74(5) | Entitles noticee to pay tax + interest + 15% penalty before adjudication to close proceedings |
| CGST Act, 2017 | S.74(9) | Mandates adjudicating officer to pass order within five years of due date of annual return |
| CGST Act, 2017 | S.75(4) | Mandates opportunity of personal hearing before adverse order is passed |
| CGST Act, 2017 | S.107 | Provides right of appeal to GST Appellate Authority within three months of order |
| CGST Act, 2017 | S.112 | Second appeal to GST Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT) |
| CGST Act, 2017 | S.132 | Prosecution provision for offences involving fraud — applies if demand exceeds threshold |
| IGST Act, 2017 | S.20 | Applies CGST provisions to inter-state supplies — Tentative; requires factual confirmation of supply type |
| CGST Rules, 2017 | Rule 142 | Prescribes Form DRC-01 (SCN), DRC-03 (voluntary payment), DRC-06 (reply format) |
| Constitution of India | Art. 226 | High Court of Telangana jurisdiction — writ if SCN is without jurisdiction or violates natural justice |

---

## 4. RELEVANT CASE LAW

- **Dhadda Exports v. Union of India** (2019) Rajasthan HC — SCN that does not specify particulars of fraud/misstatement is void for violation of natural justice; applicable where the SCN in this case lacks precise allegations.
- **Solar Industries India Ltd. v. Assistant Commissioner of CGST** (2022) Bombay HC — Held that mere non-filing of returns does not constitute "suppression" under S.74; revenue must independently establish mens rea.
- **Metl Forging Ltd. v. Union of India** (2023) Allahabad HC — Confirmed that S.74(5) benefit (15% penalty) is available only before the adjudicating authority passes order; post-order payment forfeits this concession.
- **Khoday Distilleries Ltd. v. State of Karnataka** (1995) SC — Established that SCN must disclose the case the noticee must meet; directly supports a challenge where the notice is vague.
- **Union of India v. Bharti Airtel Ltd.** (2021) SC — Held that ITC availment based on GSTR-2A data does not automatically establish wrongful claim; revenue must demonstrate actual ineligibility.

---

## 5. GOVERNMENT DATA FINDINGS

| Source | Finding | Data Point |
|---|---|---|
| GSTN Portal (API) | GSTIN Lookup | No live data — API key absent. Manual verification mandatory at gstin.gov.in |
| MeriPehchaan / DigiLocker | Citizen identity documents | Mock data only — not attributable to the taxpayer entity in this matter |
| Mee Seva TG | Certificates | Sandbox/mock data — not applicable to this GST dispute |

**Live GSTIN status for 36AABCU9603R1ZX must be verified manually at** `https://www.gst.gov.in` **→ Search Taxpayer before any filing.**

---

## 6. RECOMMENDED LEGAL STRATEGY

**Immediate Actions (0–7 days):**
- **Action 1:** Obtain certified copy of the SCN (Form DRC-01) and verify the date of issue, tax period, demand head (CGST/SGST/IGST/Cess), and the specific allegation (fraud/misstatement/suppression) — CGST Act S.74(1), Rule 142(1) — **Noticee/Advocate**.
- **Action 2:** Calculate the reply deadline (SCN mandates reply within 30 days of service) and calendar the personal hearing date — CGST Act S.75(4) — **Advocate**.
- **Action 3:** Pull all GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, GSTR-2A/2B filings for the disputed tax period from the GST portal to identify the exact discrepancy alleged — CGST Rules, Rule 59, Rule 60 — **Chartered Accountant/Tax Consultant**.

**Short-Term Actions (7–30 days):**
- **Action 1:** File a detailed written reply in Form DRC-06, specifically challenging (a) jurisdiction to invoke S.74 in absence of fraud evidence and (b) the demand computation — CGST Act S.74, Rule 142(3) — **Advocate + CA jointly**.
- **Action 2:** If tax liability is not genuinely disputed, evaluate voluntary payment of tax + interest + 15% penalty via Form DRC-03 to extinguish proceedings under S.74(5) — CGST Act S.74(5) — **Noticee with CA**.
- **Action 3:** Request and attend personal hearing before the adjudicating authority; submit written submissions simultaneously — CGST Act S.75(4) — **Advocate**.

**Medium-Term Actions (1–3 months):**
- **Action 1:** If adverse order is passed, file appeal before the GST Appellate Authority (Commissioner Appeals) in Form APL-01 within three months, depositing 10% pre-deposit — CGST Act S.107(6) — **Advocate**.
- **Action 2:** If SCN is jurisdictionally infirm (e.g., issued post limitation, or without fraud allegation), file writ petition under Art. 226 before the High Court of Telangana — Constitution of India Art. 226 — **Senior Advocate**.

---

## 7. DOCUMENTS REQUIRED

**Essential:**
- [ ] Original SCN in Form DRC-01 — Establishes the demand, tax period, and allegations; provided by revenue authority
- [ ] GSTR-1, GSTR-3B returns for disputed tax period — Primary evidentiary base; pulled from GST portal by noticee
- [ ] GSTR-2A/2B reconciliation statements — Establishes ITC eligibility; generated from GST portal
- [ ] Tax payment challans (Form PMT-06/GST PMT-07) for disputed period — Proves amounts already paid
- [ ] GST Registration Certificate — Confirms registration status and category; GSTN portal

**Supporting:**
- [ ] Purchase invoices and e-way bills for transactions in dispute — Establishes genuineness of supplies and ITC
- [ ] Bank statements for the disputed period — Corroborates transaction genuineness
- [ ] Audited financial statements / books of accounts — Reconciles turnover declared vs. assessed
- [ ] Correspondence with the Department (prior notices, replies) — Establishes procedural history

---

## 8. POTENTIAL RISKS & CHALLENGES

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |

| Limitation: S.74 order must be passed within 5 years of annual return due date; if demand is time-barred, SCN is void | Medium — depends on tax period (not disclosed) | Verify exact tax period from SCN; file preliminary objection on limitation in DRC-06 reply |
| S.74 invocation challenged as improper (no fraud element) — Revenue may not have established mens rea | High — S.74 requires positive allegation of fraud/wilful misstatement | Challenge in reply; cite Solar Industries (2022) and Khoday Distilleries (1995) |
| Prosecution risk under S.132 if demand exceeds ₹5 crore | Low–Medium — depends on quantum (not disclosed) | Ascertain demand quantum immediately; if threshold approached, retain criminal counsel |

| ITC reversal demand creating cash flow disruption | Medium | Assess DRC-03 voluntary payment option to cap penalty at 15% under S.74(5) |

---

## 9. NEXT STEPS
